papers.title: Nationwide clinical-genomic epidemiology of listeriosis in Taiwan, 2018-2025: disease manifestations in relation to clonal background.
papers.abstract: Listeriosis is an uncommon but severe foodborne infection, yet nationwide data linking pathogen genomics with clinical manifestations remain limited. We analyzed 1,252 laboratory-confirmed symptomatic listeriosis cases reported through nationwide surveillance in Taiwan during 2018-2025, with whole-genome sequencing of the corresponding clinical Listeria monocytogenes isolate from every case. The average annual incidence was 6.68 cases per 1,000,000 person-years, and 30-day all-cause mortality was 11.4%. Incidence showed an age-dependent sex pattern, with higher incidence among females aged 15-44 years and a shift toward male predominance at older ages. The female excess at ages 15-44 years persisted after exclusion of documented maternal-neonatal cases (male-to-female incidence rate ratio, 0.57; 95% confidence interval, 0.36-0.89). Clonal complex 87 (CC87) was the predominant CC (35.9%), whereas CC1 and CC2 were associated with higher odds of central nervous system (CNS) infection. LIPI-4 occurred predominantly in CC87, and LIPI-4-positive isolates showed lower odds of CNS infection; however, this association could not be separated from clonal background. More broadly, most associations of pathogenicity islands, virulence genes, and their alleles with disease manifestations could not be separated from the underlying clonal backgrounds in which these markers occurred, and none of the estimable associations remained significant after CC adjustment. This nationwide clinical-genomic study characterizes the contemporary burden of listeriosis in Taiwan and highlights clonal background as essential context for interpreting associations between virulence markers and disease manifestations.

papers.title: Advancements in understanding the pathogenic mechanisms of Treponema pallidum.
papers.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (T. pallidum) is the etiological agent of syphilis, which has been regarded as a great imitator with its multiple possible clinical manifestations. The mechanisms by which this spirochete enters the host, elicits inflammation, causes host cell damage, and persists in its natural host are not adequately understood. This review aims to briefly introduce the microbiology of T. pallidum as a unique pathogen and summarize the recent advancements in understanding the molecular basis behind the immune evasion mechanisms of this pathogen. The basic scientific discussions herein should provide a framework for understanding the clinical and epidemiological outcomes described in this review.

papers.title: Highly efficient RPA product degradation and expanded PAM recognition enable RPA-Cas3 detection of Clonorchis sinensis.
papers.abstract: Clonorchis sinensis is a major foodborne pathogen threatening aquatic food safety. Microscopy, the diagnostic standard, is laborious and often lacks sensitivity for low-intensity infections. Molecular strategies coupling isothermal amplification with CRISPR/Cas systems have attracted interest, but their reliability is often undermined by competition between amplification and detection and intrinsic limitations of Cas effectors, notably PAM dependence of Cas12a and nonspecific activation of Cas13a. To address these limitations, we used the type I-A CRISPR-Cas3 system (TsiCas3) from T. siculi. Because TsiCas3 displays trans-cleavage activity at 65 °C, a temperature that completely abolishes RPA polymerase activity, this temperature gap can be exploited to avoid interference. A one-tube, closed-reaction workflow was established where target DNA is first amplified by RPA at 37 °C for 20 min, then the temperature is raised to 65 °C. This shift simultaneously inactivates RPA polymerase and activates TsiCas3-Cascade, enabling specific amplicon recognition, trans-ssDNA cleavage, and fluorescence generation. The sequential temperature control physically separates amplification from detection, eliminates mutual interference, and requires no tube opening or reagent addition. Moreover, Cas3 efficiently and near-completely degrades the RPA amplicons, substantially reducing aerosol carryover risk. This closed-tube, contamination-resistant method provides a rapid, sensitive, field-deployable tool for C. sinensis detection and represents a practical addition to clonorchiasis control.

papers.title: Breaking the channel barrier: same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy enables seven-target respiratory virus detection on a six-channel PCR platform within 20 minutes.
papers.abstract: Respiratory pathogens with overlapping symptoms-including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, H5/H7/H10 avian influenza, and RSV-co-circulate and co-infect, demanding rapid multiplex screening at points of care. Conventional multiplex real-time PCR is constrained by hardware channel capacity (≤6), making it difficult to detect seven targets while distinguishing influenza A and B in a single tube. This work addresses the contradiction between high-order multiplexing and limited fluorescence channels without sacrificing speed or sensitivity. We developed a six-channel ultra-fast PCR platform detecting seven respiratory viruses in a single tube within 20 min, using a same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy. Influenza A and B share the FAM channel yet generate distinct melting peaks (∼12 °C difference, 84.8 °C vs. 72.3 °C), enabling accurate typing via melting curve analysis. Primers, probes, and enzymes are pre-embedded as lyophilized beads in sealed cartridges for fully automated sample-to-result operation. The assay achieved 100% detection at 5 copies/test for all targets, linearity (R 2 > 0.95) across 5-10 5 copies/test, 90-110% efficiencies, and no cross-reactivity against 39 non-target pathogens. Cartridges remained stable for 12 months at 25 °C. Validation on 271 clinical specimens showed 100% agreement with sequencing-verified single-plex qPCR. This work provides the first integration of melting-curve-based same-channel multiplexing with lyophilized cartridge technology on an ultra-fast PCR platform. By overcoming channel limitations while maintaining speed and sensitivity, the system offers a practical, field-deployable screening tool for decentralized respiratory pathogen detection in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Automated machine learning framework for interpreting paper-based biosensing of pathogens.
papers.abstract: Paper-based biosensors have emerged as a promising tool for the rapid detection of microbial contaminants. However, the interpretation of paper-based biosensor images commonly relies on manual intensity extraction and assay-specific decision criteria, while explicit thresholds for positive/negative classification are often not reported. Herein, an ML framework was developed for automated interpretation of paper-based colorimetric biosensor images across distinct paper-based biosensor studies targeting different pathogens. Using conventional normalized intensity, region-of-interest (ROI)-based descriptors, and image-only convolutional neural network approaches, within-study validation showed strong positive/negative classification performance. However, the optimized decision thresholds differed between studies, and this study-dependent shift resulted in degraded cross-study classification performance. We therefore introduced a color-space normalization approach that quantified each target signal according to its chromatic relationship with the paired positive and negative controls, rather than relying on single-channel fluorescence intensity alone. This color-space normalization improved the separation of positive and negative readouts across studies and yielded comparable decision-threshold ranges in both within-study and cross-study validation. Accordingly, the color-space normalization approach provided more stable cross-study classification than conventional single-channel normalization, ROI-based descriptors, and image-only deep learning approaches. The trained model and frozen decision threshold were applied to a separate dataset as a small proof-of-concept application. These results support ML-assisted biosensor interpretation as a means to automate image interpretation and establish more consistent decision boundaries for paper-based biosensor studies.

papers.title: Perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA) exposure, through stabilizing HIF-1α to induce VEGF/VEGFR2 autocrine signaling, promotes colorectal cancer cell proliferation.
papers.abstract: Perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA) is a persistent organic pollutant widely present in the environment and resistant todegradation. In recent years, due to its extensive use in industrial production and consumer products, PFDA continuously accumulates in organisms and has become a global public health concern. Although epidemiological data suggest a possible association between PFDA and various cancer risks, its specific carcinogenic mechanism, particularly in colorectal cancer development, remains unclear. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the effects of environmentally relevant concentrations of PFDA on the biological behavior of colorectal cancer cells and to elucidate. the underlying molecular mechanisms. In vitro, human colorectal cancer cell lines HCT116 and HT-29 were used as models. Our results demonstrated that PFDA treatment significantly enhanced the malignant phenotype of cancer cells in a dose-dependent manner. Colony formation ability was enhanced. Meanwhile, cell invasion capacity was also significantly improved. Additionally, PFDA exposure induced glycolytic metabolic reprogramming in cancer cells, a metabolic feature closely associated with rapid tumor growth and malignant progression. To further elucidate the mechanism, our team conducted in-depth molecular biological investigations. The study found that PFDA does not affect gene transcription but instead directly binds to and stabilizes the VHL protein, preventing its degradation of HIF-1α. This consequently significantly upregulates its classic downstream target genes, VEGF and its receptor VEGFR2, thereby activating key downstream pro-survival and proliferation signaling pathways. Using a nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft model, our data also confirmed that in vivo PFDA exposure promotes tumor growth, with significant increases in both tumor volume and weight. In summary, this study lays a solid foundation for further in-depth toxicological research on PFDA.

papers.title: Identifying GSTM1, SDC1, and VTN as key biomarkers and therapeutic targets for NETs in acute pancreatitis based on bioinformatics analysis and experiments.
papers.abstract: Acute pancreatitis(AP) is a severe inflammatory disease associated with high morbidity and mortality. Emerging evidence suggests that neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) play a pivotal role in AP pathogenesis; however, effective therapeutic targets and interventions remain poorly understood.We conducted weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) on two independent transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus to identify disease-associated gene modules. Differential expression analysis of NET-related genes was performed, followed by functional enrichment analysis and protein-protein interaction network construction to elucidate biological pathways. Core genes were identified using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, random forest, and support vector machine recursive feature elimination algorithms. Network pharmacology was employed to predict potential therapeutic drugs. Finally, experimental validation was conducted using a caerulein-induced AP mouse and cell model.The WGCNA analysis identified 2707 key genes. Subsequently, combining differential expression analysis with machine learning approaches, we identified three core genes: glutathione S-transferase mu 1 (GSTM1), syndecan-1 (SDC1), and vitronectin (VTN). These genes exhibited significant expression alterations in AP. Drug prediction and molecular docking analysis revealed that semaxanib demonstrated strong binding affinity to all three target proteins. Experimental validation in the AP model confirmed the bioinformatics predictions: GSTM1 and VTN were significantly downregulated, while SDC1 was markedly upregulated.We identified NETs-related genes GSTM1, SDC1, and VTN as novel biomarkers for AP. Furthermore, semaxanib may have potential associations with pathways related to GSTM1, SDC1 and VTN, thereby participating to some extent in the intervention of acute pancreatitis. These findings provide a foundation for precision medicine approaches in AP management.

papers.title: Photoelectrochemical interface mediated by S-scheme charge transfer and p-n heterojunction: Ultrasensitive detection of the emerging contaminant ornidazole.
papers.abstract: Ornidazole (ONZ) is a widely used nitroimidazole-class antibiotic whose environmental persistence due to misuse intensifies antimicrobial resistance and accelerates pathogen evolution, posing serious risks to human health and ecological safety. To address this issue, we developed a novel photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensor for ultrasensitive ONZ detection based on a p-n heterojunction between pseudobrookite-type oxide MgTi 2 O 5 and the metal-organic framework (MOF) Cu-BTC. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations corroborate the favorable band structure of the heterojunction. The built-in electric field and S-scheme charge transfer at the interface enable efficient separation of photogenerated carriers, yielding an ultralow detection limit of 0.65 pM, a wide linear range from 1 pM - 10 nM (R 2 = 0.9992), and excellent anti-interference, selectivity, stability and reproducibility. The sensor achieved 98.43% - 103.62% recovery in real samples including commercial capsules, tablets, and environmental water, demonstrating high practical reliability. This work presents a cost-effective, portable, and high-performance platform for ONZ monitoring and offers new insights into advanced PEC sensor design for antibiotic pollution detection.

papers.title: Azole resistance in Aspergillus series Nigri and possible link with environmental selection route.
papers.abstract: Resistance to medical azoles has been well investigated in Aspergillus fumigatus, which is primarily driven by exposure to azole fungicides. Azole resistance selection in other Aspergillus species remains understudied. We investigated azole resistance selection in Aspergillus series Nigri. 165 clinical series Nigri isolates were collected from Dutch and Belgian hospitals and 77 environmental isolates were obtained from air and other environmental sources, including known hotspots for azole resistance selection. Isolates were screened for resistance to medical azoles and selected fungicides using the EUCAST microbroth dilution reference method. Epidemiological cut-off values were used to identify non-wildtype isolates. All isolates were subjected to whole-genome sequencing, and global sequence databases were used for population genomic analyses. Clinical information was collected for azole-resistant isolates. Aspergillus tubingensis was the dominant species lineage among the clinical isolates (120/165, 72·7%), whereas species of the A. niger lineage were more frequently identified in environmental samples (55/78, 70·5%). Overall A. tubingensis isolates showed higher minimum inhibitory concentrations than A. niger isolates; 27 clinical isolates (17·0%) showed a non-wildtype phenotype for medical azoles as well as 24 of 78 (30·8%) environmental isolates. Sequencing revealed a worldwide distribution of multiple clonal groups. Cross resistance between medical azoles and azole fungicides was observed in A. tubingensis lineage isolates, which were recovered from hotspots, air and patient samples. Pan-azole resistant A. tubingensis was recovered from five mould-active azole-naïve patients, including a patient with proven invasive aspergillosis. Our study shows azole resistance in A. tubingensis lineage isolates and evidence that supports environmental resistance selection. Population genomics indicate a risk of global migration of resistant clones in A. tubingensis. Next to confirmative studies regarding black aspergilli, mycobiome analysis of hotspots are needed to identify potential selection of intrinsic or acquired resistant fungal species that may cause infections.

papers.title: Host-specific distribution of antimicrobial resistance in non-clinical Salmonella: a one health analysis of 791,298 isolates.
papers.abstract: The environmental distribution of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is frequently attributed to diffuse agricultural and aquatic reservoirs. To evaluate source-associated differences in AMR carriage, pre-computed genomic metadata for 791,298 Salmonella enterica isolates from the NCBI Pathogen Detection database were analyzed. Multivariate logistic regression, adjusted for serovar, geographic location, and database submission year, stratified non-clinical isolates into specific ecological niches against a human clinical baseline. Historical resistance (tetracycline) and mobilized colistin resistance (mcr) demonstrated profound concentration in poultry and swine environments. Crucially, while Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase (ESBL) carriage was negatively associated with swine, bovine, and generalized aquatic environments, poultry isolates exhibited an over four-fold increased relative prevalence (Adjusted OR = 4.03). Conversely, general aquatic environments consistently demonstrated a negative association across all resistance classes. These findings indicate that environmental AMR carriage within this database is highly compartmentalized, highlighting direct livestock production interfaces as primary targets for genomic surveillance.

papers.title: Prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening of chromosome abnormalities: A technical standard of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) and the College of American Pathologists (CAP).
papers.abstract: The American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the College of American Pathologists work group developed this technical standard to address challenges associated with laboratory validation and implementation of prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening. Given that cfDNA screening is the most sensitive and specific screening test available for common fetal aneuploidies, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine recommend that prenatal cfDNA screening be offered to all pregnant persons as a first-tier screening option, regardless of their risk status. Fetal cfDNA in maternal circulation originates from placenta-derived trophoblasts, allowing for the identification of fetuses at increased risk for trisomies 13, 18, and 21 and aneuploidy of sex chromosomes, in addition to recurrent segmental aneuploidies associated with syndromes. Multiple cfDNA analysis techniques exist, and because of the complex nature of this screening, this technical standard aims to promote uniform laboratory practices. This document deals with the technical standards applicable to prenatal cfDNA screening of chromosome abnormalities in maternal plasma. This document serves as a resource to assist clinical laboratories with the validation methods, ongoing monitoring of test quality and performance, and the interpretation and reporting of these results.

papers.title: Interpretation of NMD-Escaping Variants with Activating Mechanisms in Cancer Genes.
papers.abstract: The Clinical Genome Resource, Cancer Genomics Consortium, and Variant Interpretation for Cancer Consortium joint somatic recommendations address protein-truncating variants predicted to escape nonsense-mediated decay (NMDe), primarily in tumor suppressor genes associated with loss-of-function mechanisms. Guidance for interpreting NMDe variants that activate oncogenes and dual-function genes remains limited. We screened the Catalogue of Somatic Mutations in Cancer (COSMIC) for NMDe nonsense and frameshift variants. Our analysis focused on actionable oncogenes and dual-function genes annotated by OncoKB, integrating tumor-type context and published functional evidence, and performed gene-level variant-type modeling. A St. Jude Children's Research Hospital pediatric clinical genomics cohort served as an independent verification set. We identified 12 genes exhibiting two activating NMDe patterns: (i) frameshift NMDe variants that generate recurrent C-terminal peptide fragments altering protein interactions (e.g., CALR); and (ii) NMDe truncations that remove C-terminal inhibitory/degradation regions, increasing protein stability or signaling (e.g., PPM1D). In the pediatric cohort, 120 NMDe variants across 9 genes occurred in ∼3% (114/3,492) of unique samples, of which 119 were classified as likely oncogenic or higher. Integrating gene function, variant type, and C-terminal consequences is essential for comprehensive interpretation of somatic NMDe variants across adult and pediatric cancer cohorts.

papers.title: Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing as a Robust Diagnostic Approach for Human Orf Virus Infection Undetectable by Conventional Microbiological Methods.
papers.abstract: Orf virus (ORFV) is a significant pathogen known for its highly contagious nature. This study reports the case of a 55-year-old male farmer who developed fever and wound infection following an untreated sheep bite. The hospital utilized metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) technology to identify the rare pathogen- orf virus. Since orf virus cannot be detected through conventional bacterial and fungal cultures, this study underscores the importance of mNGS in identifying rare pathogens. The patient developed fever and wound suppuration on day 11 following a sheep-related injury and was admitted to our hospital on day 17 because of persistent intermittent fever despite prior antibiotic treatment. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed soft tissue damage. Blood cultures, Gram and Ziehl-Neelsen staining, and bacterial and fungal cultures of wound secretions yielded negative results. Subsequently, mNGS detected orf virus in the wound secretion specimen. To verify the mNGS results, a quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) analysis targeting the B2L gene of parapoxvirus was performed on the wound secretion specimen. mNGS identified ORFV in the wound secretion specimen. B2L -targeted qPCR performed on the same specimen yielded a positive result, while Sanger sequencing provided limited additional sequence-level support consistent with a parapoxvirus B2L target. Orf virus cannot be cultured in most diagnostic laboratory cell lines, and there is no routine clinical detection for orf virus. Therefore, mNGS emerges as a powerful tool for detecting such infections. This case demonstrates that mNGS provides an effective diagnostic strategy for infections that cannot be identified by traditional culture methods.

papers.title: High Throughput Sequencing vs Biological Indexing for the Detection of Viral Pathogens in Rubus.
papers.abstract: Rubus species are native to six continents and are grown commercially around the world. Production of raspberries and blackberries in the United States alone is over 100,000 metric tons. Global production and transport require prevention of both endemic and exotic diseases through clean plant programs and certification testing. While graft bioassay has been the standard in certification programs for pathogen detection, high throughput sequencing (HTS) has the potential to streamline the testing process and identify pathogens more effectively. In this study, HTS was evaluated for virus detection compared to graft bioassay in Rubus plants. Leaves from 71 donor plants were grafted onto three replicates of Rubus occidentalis 'Munger' black raspberry indicator plants and monitored for symptom expression over eight weeks and again after natural winter dormancy. Donor leaves were analyzed by HTS for the presence of viral sequences. The experiment was repeated twice with six replicates per donor plant across both experiments and 426 indicators total. HTS detected 20 virus species across all donors with up to six viruses in a single plant. Virus detection by HTS and graft bioassay did not correlate well. HTS detected viruses in 100% of donors while 45% of grafted indicators were asymptomatic by eight weeks after grafting and 61% asymptomatic after dormancy. Results indicate HTS is more effective at detecting viral infections, even when grafted plants are subject to natural dormancy.

papers.title: Correction: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing for pathogen detection of pulmonary infections in persons living with HIV.
Beyond precision to justice.
papers.abstract: Genomics has advanced rapidly, yet access remains profoundly unequal. The next revolution will not come from better sequencing alone but from a willingness to organize science around those who need it most. If genomics is to improve health, equitable access must become a scientific and ethical imperative.

papers.title: Genome sequencing in prenatal precision medicine of congenital malformations: Clinical experience from a single center.
papers.abstract: As a part of implementing genome sequencing in prenatal precision medicine at the department of Clinical Genetics and Genomics, Karolinska University Hospital, Stockholm, Sweden, we evaluated the utility of genome sequencing for prenatally detected malformations, including diagnostic yield, turnaround time and impact on current and future pregnancies. This study comprised 218 fetuses with different malformations. One hundred and two prospectively collected samples were analyzed using clinical trio genome sequencing, and if non-diagnostic, they underwent research analysis. In addition, 116 samples were collected retrospectively and included all fetuses referred for clinical trio genome sequencing during the study period. As part of the clinical routine at the time of the study, quantitative fluorescent-polymerase chain reaction and chromosomal microarray had been performed before genome sequencing in 84.9% (185/218) of cases. Clinical genome sequencing identified a molecular diagnosis in 22.5% (49/218) of the cases. Research analysis revealed two additional causative variants increasing the diagnostic yield to 23.4% (51/218). The phenotypes of the cases were divided into different groups with following diagnostic yields: 36.2% (21/58) in multisystem malformations, 30.8% (8/26) in skeletal malformations, 25.0% (14/56) in malformations in the central nervous system, 15.6% (5/32) in thoracic malformations, 11.5% (3/26) in abdominal malformations, and 0% (0/20) in other isolated anomalies. Additionally, four variants were considered potentially clinically relevant. A total of 39.2% (20/51) of the causative variants were related to a risk of recurrence. The turnaround time for clinical genome sequencing in ongoing pregnancies, when requested before gestational week 21 + 6 and prior to a parental decision on pregnancy continuation, was 12.5 ± 5 days (mean ± standard deviation, n = 40). Pregnancies with diagnostic results from genome sequencing were more likely to be terminated than those with normal results (p = 0.012, Fisher's exact test). Genome sequencing has an important role in prenatal precision medicine, since it can detect the underlying cause of prenatally detected malformations in a reasonable time. As causative chromosome aberrations were excluded in most of the cases, an even higher diagnostic yield can be expected if genome sequencing is offered as a first-line test or after a normal rapid aneuploidy detection result.

papers.title: Toward precision nanomedicine via artificial intelligence guided design and prediction.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing nanomedicine development by linking formulation variables and biological context with delivery, therapeutic efficacy, and safety. This review examines AI assisted formulation design, centralized formulation databases, prediction of nanoparticle self assembly, and models of cell and tissue selective delivery, biodistribution, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent advances in predicting nanotoxicity and nanoparticle induced immune responses further emphasize the importance of incorporating safety endpoints into nanomedicine optimization. Beyond nanocarrier engineering, foundation models and multimodal analyses of single-cell and spatial data are expanding biological discovery by characterizing disease associated cellular states, prioritizing therapeutic targets, and predicting treatment responses. Computational approaches also support the design of therapeutic RNA, peptides, proteins, and programmable protein nanomaterials. For example, mRNA sequences generated by GEMORNA and delivered via lipid nanoparticles increased erythropoietin expression in mice by up to 15-fold compared with a benchmark sequence. Integration of biological discovery with biomolecular and nanocarrier design may inform therapeutic cargo selection, targeting strategies, and functional nanomaterial development. AI may connect patient specific biological characteristics with predictions of nanomedicine delivery and therapeutic response to support patient stratification and individualized treatment selection. Integration of histological, imaging, molecular, and longitudinal data may enable treatment strategies to be adapted to differences in tissue characteristics, disease state, and therapeutic response. Emerging approaches based on digital twins and adaptive treatment control may extend the framework toward individualized dosing and dynamic treatment optimization. Major challenges include data heterogeneity, limited model generalizability, and the need for experimental and prospective validation. Progress toward precision therapy will require integrated frameworks that jointly consider delivery, efficacy, selectivity, and safety while clearly distinguishing demonstrated applications from future opportunities.

papers.title: Translocation of the environmental bacterium Aquitalea magnusonii promotes systemic inflammation and liver fibrosis in chronic liver disease.
papers.abstract: Impaired mucosal barrier integrity facilitates translocation of the gut microbiome into the circulation and the liver, thereby exacerbating the severity of chronic liver diseases (CLD). This study aimed to investigate the pathogenic role of non-commensal environmental bacteria, specifically Aquitalea magnusonii in CLD progression by assessing its ability to cross the intestinal barrier and induce systemic inflammation and liver fibrosis. Using an integrated translational framework, patient blood analyses were combined with multi-omics profiling, human intestinal epithelial models, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), hepatic stellate cells (HSC), monocytes, and alcoholic (ALD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated (MASLD) models to evaluate the translocation, virulence, inflammatory and fibrotic potential of A. magnusonii in CLD. Non-commensal environmental bacteria, including Aquitalea spp. were detected in multiple organs in both ALD and MASLD models. Detection of Aquitalea DNA in patient samples and other non-commensal environmental bacteria in tap water suggested potential aquatic reservoirs. A. magnusonii produced 12 acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) associated metabolites and its outer membrane vesicles (OMV) were enriched in virulence-related proteins, supporting roles in adhesion, invasion, and immune activation. In addition, gavage with A. magnusonii led to a substantial dysbiotic shift in the gut microbiome. Mechanistically, the cell-free supernatant of A. magnusonii culture activated TLR2- and TLR4-dependent pro-inflammatory signaling pathways. Exposure to A. magnusonii or its pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) significantly increased inflammation and fibrosis in vitro and in vivo. Non-commensal environmental bacteria, in the example of A. magnusonii, can translocate across the intestinal barrier and promote liver inflammation and fibrogenesis via metabolite production, virulence-associated OMV, and innate immune activation. This study highlights an underrecognized role of non-commensal environmental bacteria in chronic liver disease. Beyond gut commensals, detection of non-commensal environmental microbes such as Aquitalea was associated with markers of more advanced liver disease, while experimental studies of A. magnusonii support biological plausibility for a potential contributory role. These findings highlight the importance of considering environmental reservoirs and non-commensal pathogens in microbial contributions to CLD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Redundant proteolytic pathways control ribosomal protein bL27 maturation in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
papers.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a major human respiratory pathogen. The bacterial 70S ribosome is a target of many clinically important antibiotics. The N-terminus of ribosomal protein bL27 extends into the peptidyl transferase center and contributes to the translation process. In Firmicutes, full-length bL27 contains an 8-12 amino acid N-terminal extension that is absent from Gram-negative bacteria. This extension is cleaved by the protease Prp, which is absent from organisms lacking the extension. Prp-mediated cleavage of bL27 is essential in Staphylococcus aureus, and Prp has been proposed as a potential antibiotic target. Here, we show that in S. pneumoniae strain TIGR4, a Δprp mutant remained viable, and produced ribosomes containing cleaved bL27, whereas deletion of prp was not tolerated in strain D39. These results suggested the presence of an alternate bL27-processing protease in TIGR4 that was absent from D39. Using a combination of genomics, proteomics and biochemical analyses, we identified this enzyme as the product of previously uncharacterized gene SP_1145, encoding a protease that we named Ribosome rescue protease (Rrp). SP_1145 is carried on a mobile genetic element that is present in strain TIGR4, but absent from D39. Our findings shed light on an alternative mechanism for bL27 maturation, and indicate that some strains of S. pneumoniae harbor horizontally acquired redundant pathways for this essential ribosome processing step.

papers.title: Development of a quantum dot-based immunochromatographic strip for the rapid detection of H9N2 subtype avian influenza virus.
papers.abstract: H9N2 subtype avian influenza virus (H9N2 AIV) is a globally widespread poultry pathogen capable of cross-species transmission to mammals and sporadic human infection, causing severe economic losses and public health risks. In this study, the HA1 protein of H9N2 AIV was used as the target antigen. High-activity recombinant HA1 was expressed in the 293F eukaryotic system and used to prepare specific monoclonal antibodies in mice. A highly sensitive quantum dot-based fluorescent immunochromatographic strip was developed for the rapid detection of H9N2 AIV antigen. The optimal detection time was 15minutes. The strip showed excellent specificity with no cross-reactivity to H3, H10 HA1, IBDV VP2, or IBV S proteins. The visual limit of detection was 1 × 10 5.3 TCID 50 /mL, and the strip remained stable for six months under dry, sealed, room-temperature storage. Featuring simple operation, rapid detection, high sensitivity, and strong specificity, this method provides valuable technical support for the on-site rapid detection of H9N2 AIV, as well as the prevention and control of avian influenza and related poultry epidemics.

papers.title: A One-Step Multiplex Real-Time Reverse Transcription Quantitative PCR Assay for Rapid and Simultaneous Detection of Human Parainfluenza Virus, Human Metapneumovirus, and Rhinovirus in Patients with Acute Respiratory Tract Infection.
papers.abstract: Clinically, acute respiratory tract infections (ARIs) caused by human parainfluenza virus (PIV), human metapneumovirus (MPV), and human rhinoviruses (HRV) are often indistinguishable due to overlapping symptoms. This study aimed to develop a one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay for simultaneous, rapid, and accurate detection of PIV (types 1-4), MPV (subgroups A and B), and HRV (species A and B). A one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay was established for simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV in clinical specimens. Primers and probes targeted conserved genomic regions, and an internal reference gene (B2M) was included for quality assurance. The limit of detection was determined via serial dilution of standard strains. Assay specificity was verified using 14 non-target pathogens, and repeatability was evaluated across various specimen concentrations. Clinical validation involved comparison with a commercial kit, with sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, agreement rate, and Kappa coefficient calculated for assessment. A one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay was successfully developed for the simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV. The assay demonstrated a detection limit of 100 copies/mL for all three targets, expressed as the equivalent concentration in the original specimen before nucleic acid extraction; this LOD was determined under multiplex co-amplification conditions, with all three targets present in the same reaction tube at every concentration level. No cross-reactivity was observed against the 14 specified non-target pathogens under the conditions evaluated, and all eight target strains were detected. Repeatability testing showed coefficients of variation (CV) of ≤2% for Ct values at low and medium concentrations. At the individual-target level, the sensitivity of the developed assay was 98.82% for HRV, 98.55% for PIV, and 100.0% for MPV, with specificity of 100.0% for all three targets. Pooled (target-level) sensitivity and specificity were 99.06% and 100.0%, respectively, and the overall agreement with the reference method was 99.24% (260/262). The method provides a technical approach for the simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV species A and B. Its clinical utility relative to comprehensive respiratory pathogen panels remains to be established.

papers.title: Aphanomyces astaci genotype group D detected in a population of Pacifastacus leniusculus from Clitunno River in Central Italy.
papers.abstract: Crayfish plague, which is caused by Aphanomyces astaci, has a devastating impact on native European freshwater crayfish species. The present study aimed to verify whether this pathogen was present in the Clitunno River (Central Italy), where the invasive Procambarus clarkii and Pacifastacus leniusculus live in sympatry since 2020. Aphanomyces astaci was confirmed to circulate within both populations, and genotype group D was identified through real-time PCR. These results provide an additional example of horizontal transmission of this pathogen between two North American crayfish species and also represent the first report of genotype group D in P. leniusculus.

papers.title: The Therapeutic Pipeline: Future Treatments and Precision Medicine.
papers.abstract: rare interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) represent a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by various pathogenic mechanisms, clinical presentations, prognoses, and therapeutic challenges. Among these, acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD), pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), and pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis (PLCH) exemplify rare pulmonary diseases driven by distinct biological mechanisms, including lysosomal dysfunction, impaired surfactant homeostasis, and activation of the mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPK) pathways. Recent advancements in molecular biology, genomics, and translational research boosted the development of precision medicine strategies and disease-specific therapies for these conditions. this narrative review was conducted in accordance with the SANRA guidelines. A thorough literature search of the PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus databases was performed from January 2000 to June 2026. significant progress has been made in treating all three diseases. In ASMD, enzyme replacement therapy with olipudase alfa has greatly improved visceral and lung symptoms, while research in gene therapy, gene editing, and metabolic treatments is ongoing. For PAP, inhaled granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) is now the primary disease-specific treatment, now supported by phase III trial evidence for inhaled molgramostim, complemented by potential therapies such as immunomodulation, macrophage transplantation, and gene-based strategies. In PLCH, the discovery of recurrent MAPK pathway variants has supported the use of genotype-targeted treatments with BRAF and MEK inhibitors. Under these conditions, advances in molecular diagnostics, circulating biomarkers, quantitative HRCT, radiomics, and artificial intelligence (AI) are poised to enhance diagnosis, patient stratification, prognosis, and treatment decisions. ASMD, PAP and PLCH are entering into an era of precision medicine, in which disease-specific molecular mechanisms play an increasing role in guiding diagnosis and treatment. Ongoing integration of genomics, biomarkers, advanced imaging, AI, and targeted therapies could revolutionise the management of conditions such as ASMD, PAP, and PLCH, leading to better long-term patient outcomes.

papers.title: Early Treatment Failure in Patients With Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma Receiving Bispecific T-Cell Engagers: Development and Validation of the CHARGE Prognostic Index.
papers.abstract: Outcomes with bispecific T-cell engagers (TCEs) in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) are heterogeneous. A practical tool to guide prognosis is needed. We developed a model integrating clinical, biological, and treatment-related variables to predict progression-free survival (PFS) in patients receiving B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)- or G-protein-coupled receptor class 5 member D-directed TCEs. We evaluated outcomes of 577 BCMA-directed and 366 talquetamab treatments across 15 US Multiple Myeloma Immunotherapy Consortium centers. Variables significantly associated with inferior PFS in a multivariate Cox model were incorporated into a prognostic score and validated in an independent multicenter International Myeloma Foundation cohort. With a median follow-up of 8.4 months, the median PFS was 6.4 months (7.0 months for BCMA TCE; 6.1 months for talquetamab); 92% of patients were triple-class-refractory. Six variables significantly associated with inferior PFS-high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities (HRCAs) [del(17p) or ≥2 HRCAs], hyperferritinemia (≥600 ng/mL), anemia (hemoglobin <9 g/dL), early relapse (<18 months from frontline therapy), general performance status (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status ≥2), and exposure to prior BCMA-directed therapy-were combined to form the CHARGE index, stratifying patients into three risk groups. The median PFS was 21.8 months (95% CI, 11.7 to not reached), 7.1 months (95% CI, 6.1 to 10.1), and 1.6 months (95% CI, 1.2 to 2.5) in the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups, respectively; hazard ratios (HRs) were 2.0 (95% CI, 1.5 to 2.7) and 4.8 (95% CI, 3.5 to 6.7) for intermediate- and high-risk versus low-risk groups. External validation (n = 173) showed that the median PFS was not reached, 7.0 months, and 3.0 months, with corresponding HRs of 2.9 (95% CI, 1.7 to 4.9) and 4.8 (95% CI, 2.6 to 8.7). The CHARGE index provides a simplified and externally validated framework for predicting treatment outcomes in patients with RRMM receiving TCEs.

papers.title: AI-Driven Reconstruction of Online Health Narratives Using Agent-Action-Outcome Modeling: Algorithm Development and Validation.
papers.abstract: People share health experiences online as stories, not isolated facts. Most computational systems reduce these narratives to keywords or claims, overlooking the agency, causality, and interpretation that determine whether health information is safe or potentially harmful to act on. Content can use medically accurate terminology while describing unsafe behavior, rendering it invisible to fact-checking and keyword approaches. This limitation, which we term narrative blindness , constrains the ability of computational systems to extract, represent, and reason over narratives as coherent wholes. This study introduces the Narrative Builder, a computational framework that reconstructs unstructured online health stories into machine-readable agent-action-outcome (AAO) narrative graphs, preserving structural, causal, and interpretive dimensions. We formalize narrative blindness as a measurable property of natural language processing systems and evaluate whether theory-grounded reconstruction can address it. We operationalized Labov and Waletzky's sociolinguistic narrative theory within a computational AAO schema, enriched with interpretive dimensions from psychological and clinical communication frameworks. From 5386 Reddit health threads (spanning February 2019 to November 2024), 2 domain experts (a biomedical researcher and a physician) annotated a gold-standard dataset of 2000 segments from 704 threads, with interrater reliability (Krippendorff α) of 0.75 to 0.82 across all annotated tasks (0.78-0.81 for the 4 interpretive classification tasks). A dual-model architecture combining BioBERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations From Transformers for Biomedical Text Mining) with a conditional random field (CRF) layer for AAO extraction and multitask DistilBERT for interpretive classification was evaluated using 5-fold grouped cross-validation, grouped on the annotation-level key to prevent data leakage, with a separate held-out test set and a McNemar test against term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) and BioBERT-without-CRF baselines. The Narrative Builder achieved a span-level F 1 -score of 0.850 for AAO extraction on the held-out test set, with per-type F 1 of 0.90 (action), 0.83 (agent), and 0.77 (outcome), outperforming the TF-IDF baseline (0.781; P <.001). Labovian stage classification reached macro- F 1 of 0.501, and interpretive dimensions reached macro- F 1 values of 0.466 (emotion), 0.528 (stance), and 0.465 (tone). Clinical-value extraction achieved a precision of 0.90, and Unified Medical Language System concept normalization reached 100% coverage across 12,101 queries. A rule-based causal direction classifier identified 17.3% of segments as candidate outcome-to-action (inverted) patterns, though validation showed limited precision (0.277), and this distribution is reported as exploratory. Single-rater expert review of generated graphs indicated narrative coherence (mean 0.89, SD 0.08) and medical plausibility (mean 0.91, SD 0.07). The Narrative Builder reads health stories as coherent wholes rather than isolated facts, producing AAO narrative graphs that retain the agents, actions, outcomes, and emotional framing that determine how individuals interpret and act on health information. By formalizing narrative blindness as a measurable property and reconstructing narrative structure with strong extraction performance, this work establishes narrative reconstruction as a feasible complement to fact-based health informatics, providing structured input for downstream credibility assessment.

papers.title: Three-Year Polymerase Chain Reaction-Based Surveillance of Respiratory Tract Infections in Adults and Seasonal Patterns.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the aetiological composition, seasonal variation and risk factors of adult respiratory tract infections in Ganzhou, Jiangxi Province, during 2023-2025. A total of 8,493 adults (≥18 years) with respiratory symptoms were enrolled from a tertiary hospital during 2023-2025. Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were tested using multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panels targeting six categories of seven respiratory pathogens: influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus types I and III, adenovirus and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Mixed infections (two or more pathogens) were reported separately. Data were analysed by univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression. The overall pathogen detection rate was 4.14% (352/8,493), comprising 325 single infections (92.33%) and 27 mixed infections (7.67%). Among single infections, M. pneumoniae (39.69%), influenza A virus (28.00%) and RSV (16.00%) predominated. Infections peaked in winter-spring (December-March). Age ≥65 years (OR = 2.35, 95% CI: 1.78-3.09), underlying diseases (OR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.89-3.08) and emergency department admission (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.24-2.01) were independent risk factors. Adult respiratory infections in Ganzhou show clear winter-spring seasonality, with M. pneumoniae, influenza A virus and RSV as leading pathogens. These findings support seasonally targeted surveillance - with enhanced monitoring for M. pneumoniae and influenza during winter-spring months - and prioritised vaccination, expanded diagnostic panels and early PCR-based diagnosis for adults aged ≥65 years and those with underlying diseases, thereby strengthening local respiratory infection prevention and control strategies.

papers.title: LUNA-FM: a subword foundation model for long non-coding RNAs for functional inference.
papers.abstract: RNA foundation models (FMs) have shown promise for RNA identification and functional annotation. However, many use single-nucleotide tokenization, which produces long input sequences and can increase computational costs when modelling long RNAs, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). To address these limitations, we introduce LUNA-FM ( Length-efficient s U bword-based N ucleic A cid F oundation M odel) , an RNA language model pretrained on approximately 28 million redundancy-filtered ncRNA sequences. LUNA-FM combines subword tokenization with a long context transformer, enabling efficient modelling of long RNA transcripts. We systematically evaluate tokenization strategies and vocabulary sizes to investigate the trade-offs between sequence compression, representation granularity, computational efficiency, and downstream performance. Across multiple RNA prediction tasks, including transcript classification, subcellular localization, and RNA-protein interaction prediction, LUNA-FM achieved competitive performance compared with existing RNA FMs while reducing effective input length and fine-tuning cost. We also found that frequency-based subword tokenization generally produced more stable and effective representations than likelihood-based approaches, although the optimal vocabulary size remained task dependent. Training-set motif discovery identified candidate motifs enriched relative to matched low-attribution and dinucleotide-shuffled controls of preeclampsia-associated lncRNAs. Overall, our findings highlight the task-dependent effects of subword tokenization and vocabulary size, extend RNA FM evaluation to longer transcript inputs, and establish LUNA-FM as a competitive model with favourable recorded fine-tuning times.

papers.title: Translating pathogen biology into diagnostic and management strategies for gummy stem blight in cucumber production.
papers.abstract: Gummy stem blight (GSB) is a major disease of cucurbits caused by Stagonosporopsis spp. and is increasingly problematic in intensive cucumber production systems, particularly where warm, humid environments favour infection, sporulation and rapid disease spread. GSB can infect vegetative and reproductive tissues and remain latent in fruit for several days before visible symptoms develop, creating a distinctive commercial challenge: disease may be difficult to detect before harvest yet cause significant post-harvest losses, reducing grower and retailer confidence. Compounding these problems, current diagnostic tools for detecting pre-symptomatic infection are often insufficiently validated for species specificity, sensitivity, turnaround time, cost, crude-sample compatibility and practical use by production staff. Many of these limitations reflect the relative lack of genomic resources for Stagonosporopsis. Therefore, this review integrates evidence from other pathosystems with current knowledge of Stagonosporopsis taxonomy, infection biology, epidemiology, diagnostics, fungicide resistance, effector biology and host resistance to identify pathways towards grower-ready tools. Specifically, we focus on how recent advances in genomics, paired with previously designed detection systems such as loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) and clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats/CRISPR-associated proteins (CRISPR/Cas), could be adapted for species-specific detection of the causal pathogen and, simultaneously, provide a regional profile of fungicide resistance. In parallel, we explore how a deeper functional genomic understanding of the disease, particularly of effector proteins expressed during the early stages of infection, could provide valuable insights into the dynamics of this host-pathogen interaction and support strategies to disrupt these interactions through novel fungistatic compounds and the development of disease-resistant cultivars. Together, these approaches could support a staged technology-development and adoption roadmap for more precise, rapid and sustainable GSB management in cucumber production.

papers.title: GSH/pH Dual-Responsive Zwitterionic mRNA Nanocomplexes for Tumor-Enriched mRNA Delivery in a B16F10 Melanoma Model.
papers.abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapy offers a programmable route to melanoma treatment, but its translation is limited by nuclease degradation, off-target biodistribution and endolysosomal trapping. Here we report a glutathione (GSH)/pH dual-responsive mRNA nanocomplex (mRNA-NC) fabricated by one-pot in situ polymerization of N-(3-aminopropyl)methacrylamide (APMA), 1-vinylimidazole (VI), N,N'-bis(acryloyl)cystamine (BACA), and 2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC) on the mRNA template. At an N/P ratio of 40, the carrier reached an encapsulation efficiency of 92.7 ± 2.1% and a loading capacity of 87.4 ± 3.2 μg mg-1, forming monodisperse particles of 126.4 ± 7.2 nm (polydispersity index, PDI, 0.14). The zwitterionic corona limited plasma protein adsorption to 12.6 ± 1.5 μg mg-1 (4.6-fold lower than jetPEI/mRNA), kept hemolysis at 0.8 ± 0.2%, and extended the serum half-life of the mRNA to ≈27.4 h, roughly 9-fold longer than naked mRNA. Release was gated by both triggers: 86.5 ± 3.7% of the cargo was released within 8 h under 10 mM GSH, whereas leakage under physiological conditions remained ≤ 12%; in a 4 h matrix, pH 5.5 plus 10 mM GSH released 85 ± 6.8% versus 12 ± 1.5% at pH 7.4 without GSH. In B16F10 cells, the nanocomplex was taken up in a dose- and energy-dependent manner, entered the lysosomal compartment, and escaped over time in a manner consistent with imidazole-mediated proton-sponge buffering (a hypothesis; intralysosomal pH was not measured directly), producing a peak firefly luciferase (FLuc) expression of 56,140 ± 3280 RLU mg-1 protein at 24 h, about 1.5-fold higher than jetPEI/mRNA, with 93.6 ± 3.9% cell viability and 6.7 ± 1.2% lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release. In B16F10-bearing albino C57BL/6 mice, a single intravenous dose produced tumor-dominant bioluminescence (peak 5.7 × 106 photons s-1 at 6 h), a tumor enrichment index of 1.22 ± 0.18 (vs 0.31 ± 0.03 for jetPEI/mRNA) and 2.42 × 107 FLuc mRNA copies μg-1 tumor RNA at 12 h, while all 7-day safety indicators remained at phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) levels. These results demonstrate that a single zwitterionic nanocomplex can integrate stealth, dual-triggered release, and endosomal escape for safe, tumor-enriched mRNA delivery. While this study focuses on delivery performance and reporter gene expression, it lays a solid foundation for future therapeutic applications with functional mRNA.

papers.title: MicroDUET: a dual-headed genomic foundation model for pathogen surveillance
papers.abstract: Pathogen genomic surveillance works from raw reads, assembled genomes and alignments, representations that are slow and costly to compare at scale. Compact embeddings from genomic language models offer an alternative, but surveillance requires resolving both evolutionary ancestry (phylogeny) and phenotypic capability (function) - which need not co-vary. Here we present MicroDUET, which adapts a 26.6-million-parameter ProkBERT backbone with two 3.5-million-parameter adapter heads: a phylogeny head trained contrastively on genome windows from the same microbes, and a function head trained to identify genes across taxa. On held-out retrieval benchmarks, the phylogeny head returned the correct species for 80.3% and 66.6% of cellular and viral queries, and the function head the correct gene family for 97.3% and 97.2%, reaching 74.4% accuracy on an independent antimicrobial resistance-class benchmark. Across all three benchmarks MicroDUET outranked 17 other genomic encoders. Without training on lineage, clade or drug-susceptibility tasks, MicroDUET identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis and mpox virus lineages and clades (0.965, 0.975 accuracy), discriminated rifampicin resistance without lineage adjustment (AUROC 0.985), and retrospectively identified an emerging mpox lineage as anomalous (AUROC 0.974). MicroDUET operates 10^3 - 10^4 times faster than single-threaded sequence-based alignments. MicroDUET therefore provides a compact, reusable representation for scalable pathogen surveillance and sequence triage.

papers.title: Large language models complement established workflows for mechanistic model construction and refinement in systems biology
papers.abstract: Mechanistic models provide a framework for describing, understanding, and predicting biological processes, but their development requires an interdisciplinary team with expertise in biology, mathematics, and computation. Here we present Octomod, a multi-agent workflow based on large language models (LLMs) that integrates biological knowledge retrieval, model construction, parameter estimation, and hypothesis testing. Built on established software tools, including AMICI and pyPESTO, and community standards, including SBML and PEtab, Octomod supports model development and refinement through natural-language interaction with a user. The agents' proposals must pass defined checks and the user's decision before they are used. Every input, model, check, and decision is recorded, so that model building remains transparent and reproducible. We applied Octomod to four problems. Three used published data and differ in model size and in how much the user guided the run: Octomod constructed a model that matched a published model without user guidance, supported the interactive refinement of a gene-regulatory model, and built models of cell-cell communication that explained the responses of five immune cell types to different stimuli. In the fourth application, on newly generated and unpublished lipidomics data, Octomod helped to determine which processes the measurements could inform, identify unresolved label fluxes, and reduce a supplied model to those processes. Together, these results show how LLMs can strengthen and complement established workflows for constructing and refining biologically informed models.

papers.title: Systematic benchmarks reveal DNA polymerase combinations for high-quality genome assembly
papers.abstract: Background: A fundamental challenge in biodiversity genomics is generating long-read sequencing data and high-quality genome assemblies from samples lacking gold-standard flash-frozen tissue, including ethanol-preserved specimens, minimally invasive biopsies, and small-bodied organisms. Amplification-based library preparation enables long-read sequencing of such samples, but assembly quality critically depends on the polymerase used for amplification. Results: We present a systematic benchmark of eleven long-range DNA polymerases for PacBio HiFi sequencing and genome assembly across three taxonomically diverse species: a springtail, a sea slug, and a bat. We show that polymerase choice substantially affects assembly contiguity and gene completeness, primarily caused by polymerase-intrinsic GC-dependent amplification bias and read coverage heterogeneity. Five polymerases consistently produced assemblies with comparatively high contiguity and completeness, with some enzymes outperforming the polymerase currently used in the PacBio Ampli-Fi protocol. Importantly, combining reads amplified with different polymerases frequently resulted in superior assemblies, because polymerases complement each other by covering regions where others drop out. Combining reads amplified with different polymerases, we generated haplotype-resolved assemblies of the ~1 Gb giant springtail and ~2 Gb bat genome and improved the sea slug reference genome. Using the human GIAB benchmark, we further show that optimized amplification strategies improve variant-calling accuracy, highlighting their utility in medical and clinical research. To facilitate polymerase benchmarking across additional taxa, we provide the polymeval pipeline (https://github.com/casparbein/polymeval), which automates the computational workflow. Conclusion: Our study demonstrates that optimized amplification-based HiFi sequencing generates assemblies with >1 Mb contig N50 and >90% gene completeness, providing a toolkit to produce long-read genome assemblies from challenging samples.

papers.title: EsViritu is a sensitive and specific profiler for viral pathogen detection and genome recovery in metagenomes
papers.abstract: Metagenomic sequencing allows for detection of any number of pathogenic viruses from a single sample without a priori knowledge of its contents. This has created a substantial opportunity to characterize pathogens in humans and their environment, but the field is held back by a lack of bioinformatics tools for taxonomic profiling and reconstructing virus genomes. The ideal profiler would simultaneously do two things: report viruses at single-read sensitivity so that ultra-low-abundance pathogens are not missed and hold near-perfect specificity so that a pathogen is never falsely reported. Here we present EsViritu, a taxonomic profiler that pairs an iterative greedy clustering algorithm and lowest-common-ancestor taxonomic refinement with a curated Virus Pathogen Database to reconstruct virus genomes and generate virome profiles directly from reads. We benchmarked EsViritu against four leading metagenomic profilers (Kraken2, Centrifuger, Metabuli, and Sylph), running each program across a full parameter sweep and against the same Virus Pathogen Database for an apples-to-apples comparison. Across synthetic positive controls, pathogen-free negative controls, and mutated mock communities, EsViritu was the most accurate tool at reconstructing community composition: it led or tied every tool on relative abundance accuracy at all taxonomic ranks and led or tied on detection across ranks. Importantly, other tools frequently report the presence of multiple related taxa when only reads for a single genome are present, but EsViritu faithfully records the correct, single taxon and genome. EsViritu achieves read-level sensitivity for sequences as low as 85% average nucleotide identity to the nearest reference and reports essentially no false positives in pathogen-free host and synthetic samples. EsViritu also returns reconstructed consensus genomes whose nucleotide identity to the nearest reference closely tracks ground truth, yielding both a profile and genomes from a single run.

papers.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
papers.abstract: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. Across both mutational effect prediction and drug-target affinity tasks, current AI models produce largely ligand-invariant predictions despite experimentally distinct inhibitor-dependent fitness landscapes. Ligand-aware geometric models, including LigandMPNN and LASErMPNN, partially recover experimentally validated resistance-associated hotspots, highlighting the importance of explicitly modeling protein-ligand interactions and local structural flexibility. In contrast, deep learning affinity prediction models underestimate mutation-induced changes in binding affinity. This deficiency likely reflects mutation-invariant structural priors derived from co-folded structure prediction frameworks and the absence of mutation-conditioned supervision in current affinity datasets. Finally, we further extended our analysis to several kinase-inhibitor deep mutational scanning datasets and confirm the overall trends. Our findings suggest that a primary limitation in improving performance on this task lies in the scarcity of mutation-conditioned protein-ligand training data rather than model architecture alone.

papers.title: Development of an exploratory taxonomy of veterinary AI query types and stage-specific query preferences: an expert panel study
papers.abstract: Background/objectives: The integration of large language model (LLM)-based AI tools into veterinary clinical practice is rapidly increasing; however, veterinary-specific frameworks for organizing AI query types and examining stage-specific preferences remain limited. This study aimed to develop an exploratory taxonomy of veterinary AI query types and to characterize veterinarians' stage-specific query preferences through a structured expert-panel survey. Methods: Candidate query types were drafted with the assistance of a locally deployed LLM from a preliminary review of de-identified veterinary AI chatbot query logs and refined through literature review. In a structured online survey, 43 veterinarians then selected the Clinical Support query types (A-H) they would prefer to direct to AI at each of five clinical stages and indicated preferred response formats; the survey measured self-reported query preferences, not observed use. Results: A taxonomy of 3 categories and 21 subtypes was established: Clinical Support Queries (Types A-H), Evidence-Based Research Queries (Types I-L), and Terminology and Drug Reference Queries (Types M-U). Across stages, Type B (Differential Reasoning) was most often ranked first (64/213 first-choice responses), and Type D (Clinical Decision Support) was most often ranked first for the post-consultation stage (21/42, 50.0%). In analyses accounting for repeated measures using generalized estimating equations, respondents with >=10 years of experience more often ranked Type G (Evidence Search) first than those with <10 years (OR 3.09, 95% CI 1.11-8.59; unadjusted p = 0.031), but this contrast was not significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across four contrasts (adjusted p = 0.062). Respondents from university/teaching hospitals (n = 7) ranked Type G first in 14 of 33 responses, compared with 10 of 135 responses from secondary referral hospitals (OR 9.27, 95% CI 2.94-29.22;

papers.title: deepTools4: Faster, Scalable, and Modernized Genomic Data Analysis
papers.abstract: The deepTools suite is widely used for quality control, summarization, and visualization of high-throughput sequencing data. However, as genomic datasets grow in scale and depth, existing tools often become computational bottlenecks. We present deepTools4, a modernized framework designed for high performance, scalability, and enhanced usability, while maintaining seamless integration with the Galaxy platform. Core functionality has been rewritten and thoroughly benchmarked, achieving substantial computational speed-ups. Visualization tools have been modernized to provide more intuitive, high-quality graphical outputs. In addition, our testing framework has been expanded to facilitate continuous development and ensure robustness. We demonstrate the utility of deepTools4 across diverse epigenomics and transcriptomics datasets, highlighting its ability to summarize genome-wide signals, apply a wide range of common normalization methods, and visualize enrichment patterns. The enhanced deepTools4 framework delivers a faster, more scalable solution for reproducible genome-wide analysis and interpretation across many sequencing modalities. Availability: https://github.com/deeptools/deepTools/

papers.title: Learning the limits of protein structure models with NMR chemical shifts
papers.abstract: Protein foundation models are intended to implicitly learn the chemical rules underlying protein function. However, systematically evaluating what biochemistry these models have learned remains difficult, as most downstream tasks lack experimental data fine-grained enough to expose their failure modes. NMR chemical shifts fill this gap: as direct per-atom reporters of local chemical environment, they offer a sensitive probe of structure-based representations. In this work, we present a systematically curated chemical shift dataset designed to minimize experimental confounders. We use it to benchmark diverse protein foundation models in their ability to predict backbone 15N chemical shifts, atoms that are known to be sensitive to many effects. The largest error across all models is in core residues with evidence of fast-timescale dynamics, which we investigate mechanistically using molecular dynamics simulations. Given the biological relevance of structured dynamic regions, we trained a new model based on the best of these embeddings, SLAE, to predict its own error. SLAE-ERR achieves a mean absolute error of 0.76 ppm for predicting error. Together, we hope that the datasets, evaluation tasks, and models presented here are sources of guidance for protein design model improvement.

papers.title: ModBERT: a DNA modification and genetic variant-aware DNA large language model
papers.abstract: The development of foundation models that learn a general grammar of DNA (DNA language models) has accelerated in recent years. The vast majority of DNA large language models (LLMs), such as DNABERT-2 and Nucleotide Transformer, are pretrained almost exclusively on reference genomes. They therefore cannot represent the two sources of variation most directly tied to regulatory differences between people: genetic variants and DNA methylation. Long-read sequencing (Nanopore and PacBio) now measures both from the same native DNA molecules, but no model is designed to use this joint readout. With this in mind, we developed ModBERT, a DNA language model built on a five-letter probabilistic genome representation in which each position is a distribution over A, C, G, T, 5mC (represented with M). In pretraining, these distributions encode population allele frequencies and CpG methylation levels from 242 individuals in the 1000 Genomes Long-Read Sequencing Consortium, learned with a soft-target masked language modeling objective. We further propose probabilistic fine-tuning, in which the same representation encodes one individual's genotype and methylation. A fine-tuned model can then make person-specific predictions from a single assay. Under this novel fine-tuning framework, we show that ModBERT effectively utilizes methylation information to classify peaks from functional genomic assays, including histone mark (n=11 different marks) and transcription factor binding (n=69 TFs) ChIP-seq data, outperforming ab initio trained models and ModBERT pretrained on sequences without methylation. In silico methylation perturbations yield TF sensitivities that correlate with independent methylation-aware motif models. Using an evaluation design that separates generalization to new loci from generalization to new individuals, ModBERT predicts chromatin accessibility at held-out loci in held-out individuals (AUROC 0.88). Its predicted variant effects agree with likely causal caQTLs (Spearman correlation = 0.52) but not with variants associated only through linkage, a traditionally challenging task. Overall, ModBERT establishes a framework for personal-genome language modeling, in which a model reads each individual's genetic and epigenetic sequence rather than a shared reference. This enables in silico dissection of variant and methylation effects on gene regulation and principled prioritization of candidates for experimental validation as population-scale long-read cohorts (e.g., 1KGP and Human Pangenome Reference Consortium) grow.

papers.title: DynamicsPLM: A Dynamics-Enriched Small Protein Language Model for Protein Variant Effect Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting how mutations impact protein function and stability remains a key challenge in computational biology. Current state-of-the-art protein language models (PLMs) primarily scale parameter size on sequence corpora to capture evolutionary constraints but remain blind to the explicit physical dynamics of folded proteins. Conversely, models trained strictly on physical dynamics neglect critical evolutionary sequence statistics. In this paper, we bridge this gap by introducing DynamicsPLM, a highly parameter-efficient 35-million-parameter model that unifies evolutionary and biophysical representation learning. Utilizing a second-stage, multi-task continual pretraining strategy on over 60,000 proteins, we enrich a foundational sequence encoder with explicit residue-level and pairwise molecular dynamics heads while preserving its original evolutionary knowledge. At inference, DynamicsPLM computes zero-shot mutation effects from sequence alone by balancing an evolutionary plausibility score against a structural dynamics disruption score. Across the massive ProteinGym benchmark and natural variants of the Tsuboyama folding stability dataset, DynamicsPLM achieves state-of-the-art accuracy among all models under 100M parameters, and matches or outperforms several billion-scale sequence-based models of its size. Our findings demonstrate that explicit structural-dynamics supervision provides a parameter-efficient alternative to raw scale. Availability: All codes including data preparation scripts, training and validation recipes, and experimental configurations for LoMuS are available at: https://github.com/kabir-ai2bio-lab/DynamicsPLM.

papers.title: Binary Patterning as a Probe of Protein Language Model Representations
papers.abstract: Do protein language models (pLMs) encode the physical rules that govern protein folding? The four-helix bundle provides a classic test case because binary patterning, the ordered placement of polar and nonpolar residues along an amphipathic -helix, is sufficient to generate folded proteins with high probability. Here, we ask whether ESM2 captures the sequence grammar underlying this design strategy. Libraries of synthetic sequences constrained only by binary patterning were predicted by ESMFold to form four-helix bundles. Predicted helicity, compactness, and topological diversity changed with sequence length in the same direction as experimentally characterized libraries, although the model did not distinguish successful from unsuccessful individual designs. Principal component analysis of ESM2 embeddings revealed representations of hydrophobic patterning, helix-loop boundaries, and heptad register. Extending the analysis to all 128 heptad binary patterns produced a jellyfish-shaped manifold in which hydrophobic composition formed the dominant axis, while paired components encoded pattern phase. Manifold geometry depended on amino-acid chemistry, repeat number, and linker sequence, and collapsed when amino acids were assigned to arbitrary categories. ESM2 therefore combines general repeat recognition with protein-specific physicochemical information. More broadly, synthetic sequence libraries provide experimentally grounded probes of protein language model representations and their relationship to protein biophysics.

papers.title: High-Performance All-Atom Continuous Constant-pH Molecular Dynamics and Native Asynchronous Replica Exchange in Amber
papers.abstract: Conformational dynamics of biomolecules, including proteins and nucleic acids, are often coupled to changes in protonation states. All-atom particle-mesh Ewald continuous constant-pH molecular dynamics (PME-CpHMD) enables proton-coupled dynamics, but its routine use has been limited by computational cost. Here we report a second-generation CUDA implementation of PME-CpHMD in Amber, in which the CpHMD-specific nonbonded corrections are evaluated in a separate kernel. Across protein systems ranging from 45 to 1,338 residues, the new implementation increases throughput by 1.5-2 fold relative to the previous fused-kernel implementation and limits the overhead relative to conventional MD to 12-18%. We also implemented the asynchronous pH replica-exchange (pH-REX) algorithm natively in pmemd.cuda.MPI, allowing simulations to run on fewer GPUs than replicas without the overhead of the previous Python wrapper. Furthermore, we derived CpHMD titration parameters for all six titratable residue types (Asp, Glu, His, Cys, Tyr, and Lys) for use with three protein force fields: CHARMM c22/CMAP, Amber ff14sb and ff19sb. The new implementations and parameterization were validated using pKa calculations of model peptides and hen egg white lysozyme (HEWL). The HEWL simulations revealed force-field-specific limitations, including overestimation of the pKa downshift 20 of H15 and sensitivity of the proton donor assignment in coupled E35/D52 dyad. Comparison with our previous work and the PME-CpHMD simulations in GROMACS with the CHARMM c36m force field demonstrated the robustness and sampling efficiency of pH-REX PME-CpHMD simulations. The new implementation provides a foundation for routine all-atom constant-pH simulations in Amber. The analysis highlights the need for continued development of protein force fields to more accurately balance intramolecular electrostatics and solvation of charged residues.

papers.title: bofasa enables high-quality orthology inference across diverse multi-species bacterial genome sets
papers.abstract: Bacterial species can be separated by billions of years of evolution. However, studies of such ancient relationships often rely on methods developed for eukaryotes, which are less diverse. Such methods can regard instances of horizontal gene transfer as contamination, rely heavily on a species phylogeny when partitioning paralogs, and fail to account for the multi-domain architectures of some genes. Here, we introduce, showcase, and benchmark bofasa, a software for high-quality and automated inference of ortholog groups across distantly related bacterial species. bofasa employs a recursive algorithm to split coarse homolog groups into paralogous subsets and first establishes domain-level ortholog groups prior to assessing evolutionary relationships between entire proteins.
